rows.why: Two of the rows, "2d" = 172800000 and "1d0h0m0s0ms" = 86400000, only work if there is a 'd' unit and a day is 24 hours. Item 7 asks exactly that, and its pick adds 'd' as 86,400,000 ms. The "0s" row also touches item 9, whose pick accepts zero values, so it agrees too.
Item 1 asks whether whitespace around the string is accepted. Its pick trims with strings.TrimSpace, so "  45m\n" parses to 2700000 as the scenario expects.

S3 covers several questions at once: empty input (item 2), a bare number (item 3), fractions (item 4), signs (item 5) and leading zeros (item 9). Item 9 is the closest because the "05s" row is the least obvious call in the list. Item 9's pick accepts leading zeros ("007s" -> 7000), but S3 expects "05s" to be rejected. The picks for items 2, 4 and 5 agree. Item 3 also rejects, but its error text "missing or unknown unit" doesn't clearly contain "duration".
No item asks whether one component's count can exceed the next unit up, as in 90m instead of 1h30m. Item 6 is about unit order and repeats, not about how big a count can be.
Item 6 asks about units out of order or used twice. Its pick requires units to go strictly from largest to smallest, each at most once, so all four examples are rejected.
Item 8 asks about the upper limit. Its pick caps at 2^53-1 ms, so 104249991d8h59m991ms = 9007199254740991, which equals the cap, is accepted.

Item 8's pick returns 0 with an error when the total goes over 2^53-1. It checks digit accumulation, each unit's multiply and the running sum, which covers both the just-over-the-cap row and the huge-number row.

Item 11 asks how FormatDuration splits a value into units. Its pick uses d, h, m, s and ms and leaves out zero parts, which gives 1m30s, 1h30m, 1d and 1d1h1m1s1ms as expected. The 0 -> "0ms" row is item 10, which also agrees.
Item 11's pick never uses a unit bigger than days, so the largest value formats as 104249991d8h59m991ms instead of rolling up into weeks or years.
No item asks whether formatting and then parsing gives the original number back. That depends on several choices together, not on any single open question.
Item 12 asks what FormatDuration does with negative or oversized values. Its pick returns "" and an error below 0 or above 2^53-1, which covers all four example values.
